verdict: No conclusion falls, but three of the four need rewording before the report is final. Conclusion 1 STANDS WITH REWORDING: the tradable-order numbers (v10 32-37%, PRESET_A 11-19%) are confirmed by my own independent event loop (bit-for-bit equal to eng.py) and by black-box perturbation, but the sentence 'the original backtest sizes the Korean night with the later US session' is an inference that sits under a '(확인됨)' tag, and the table's 'reported 58.4% vs reproduced 57.7%' compares different end dates (like-for-like the eng.py look-ahead run is about 6.5pp short of the upload, not 0.7pp); new package-internal evidence I found (the upload's own '0.47 x previous-day US intraday' statistic) supports the inference and should be cited. Conclusion 2 STANDS WITH REWORDING: '0 of 12 pass' is correct under the registered rules and survives every lever I tried, but 'PRESET_A at its most favourable equals v1 (+0.5~+1.2)' is wrong (that is the conservative basis C at the registered fee), and 'v9/v10 are below v1' is true only on the two MS1 bases; on the real-night windows the report's own table shows v9-US above v1 through 2014 with 16-20pp shallower drawdown, and its sign after 2015 depends on the fee (-1.3pp at 0.83bp, +6.2pp at the report's own 'realistic' 0.30bp). Conclusion 3 STANDS WITH SUBSTANTIAL REWORDING: 'the salvageable part is small' stands, but the report is too generous to T5: T5 fails the registered rules under both C and M (so it is not even 'conditional' by rule 4), the 'four windows' are three nested pre-2015 windows plus the holdout window, no window is statistically significant (t 0.5-1.4), the holdout +1.8pp is used as support against PRECOMMIT rule 5, and '+1~+2.5%p expected' is the best defensible case, not an expectation. Conclusion 4 STANDS (only the margin figure needs a label and the whole-contract number). I found no look-ahead or accounting error in eng.py, ntilt.py or ms1f.py, and every stored number I recomputed matched exactly.

Own scripts (all in /home/user/onv/wf3/skeptic/, run with /home/user/onv/venv/bin/python -B): s1_align.py (kr_n definition on 4,038 rows, correlations with the US session inside the night vs known at entry, reproduction of the section 1 table, like-for-like end date); s2_indep.py (my own plain-Python event loop compared with eng.py for v9, v10, PRESET_A in tradable and look-ahead modes: max relative difference 0.0; 3,629 KR entries checked for information date; black-box perturbation of eng.py on 4 nights; third 'entry-row' reading); s3_ms1.py (v1 reference 16.159% / 31.081%; T5 and P3 stored numbers for seeds 11, 1, 2 on both bases: difference 0; cash-interest lever; ntilt pulse test 30 days x 3 gates = 90 runs; future-reshuffle and volatility-lag tests for ntilt and ms1f); s4_windows.py (T5 minus v1 on the 6 reported and 6 non-overlapping real-night windows at 0.83, 1.66 and 0.30bp, paired t-statistics; stored window values reproduced exactly); s5_facts.py (night premium statistics, tail nights, KR share, Oct-Nov 2026, ms1f lag test with a -25% shock); s6_rowpair.py (fingerprint of the upload's own regression under the two row readings); s7_mech.py (12 time-shuffles of KR nights, tally of nights cut by a cooldown that began after entry); s8_spy.py (SPY 1993-98 night premium vs tick marking); s9_m96.py (mode M with premium from 1996); s10_pfee.py (P presets on real-night windows at 0.83/0.60/0.30bp and with brake delay 2); s11_cmode.py (what mode C implies for a 1x night futures position by era); s12_carry.py and s13_combo.py (carry-neutral version of C, alone and with cash interest). open_points: The original engines g2.py, uni.py and ext.py were not uploaded, so 'the original backtest stored the Korean night on its exit row' remains an inference. It is now supported by three things (order of operations in plan.py, numeric match of the look-ahead reproduction at 58-65% against about 64% like-for-like, and the upload's own '0.47 x previous-day US intraday' statistic), with one unmatched fingerprint (v10 in 2022). The files would settle it.

The real all-in MNQ cost per side, including slippage at the open and close, is unmeasured, and the verdicts on v9-US and T5 change sign inside the plausible range: v9-US against v1 in 2015-2026 is -1.3pp at 0.83bp, +1.9pp at 0.60bp and +6.2pp at 0.30bp; T5 is +1.8pp at 0.83bp, -2.7pp at 1.66bp and +4.8pp at 0.30bp.
Opening-print uncertainty of about 0.5bp per day between vendors is the same size as T5's edge; no real MNQ or KOSPI 200 futures prices were available.
The pre-1999 Nasdaq 100 night premium cannot be observed. The SPY evidence is robust only from 1996; whether the premium is taken to start in 1993 or 1996 decides whether T5 is positive under M.

My sensitivity runs used 1 to 3 seeds (carry-neutral C: seeds 11 and 1; cash interest and 1996 start: seeds 11, 1, 2; both levers on P3 at fee x2: seeds 11 and 1), not the 30 seeds of the stored results. The directions are clear; the second decimals are not.

With both non-registered levers (carry-neutral synthetic night and cash interest at rf-2%p) P3 at double fee is about break-even with v1 (-0.2 / +0.8 and -0.6 / +3.9 on two seeds). I did not run 30 seeds or the brake-delay variant under those levers, so I cannot say whether P3 would pass rules 1 and 2 under them; it would still be far below v1 on real-night data after 2001 (15.3% vs 18.9%) and in 2015-2026 (14.6% vs 28.1%).

The innocent entry-row reading of plan.py gives 42.1% for v10 to 2025-12-31 against 34.1% for the tradable order. I did not decompose the 8pp difference; that reading books the Korean night's P&L ahead of the same row's US legs, which is itself a look-ahead of a few hours.
The holdout is spent for these 12 candidates and ends 2026-08-31, before the Oct-Nov 2026 fall. Whether it was computed only once cannot be verified from the files.

Margin rates, account interest and the split between the overseas and domestic futures accounts are not verifiable without the broker screen; the 8,228만 and my 7,100만 figure are both arithmetic from the report's stated rates.

Not re-verified by me: stored numbers for candidates other than T5 and P3, the 'fake Korean leg +4.7%p' test, the Kelly estimates, the last-month losses of the three presets, live-code defects other than KILL/HALT and permanent HALT, and the effect of the yearly tax payment on the brake's drawdown reference in ms1f.py.
